newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean students admit beating man who died.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean students admit beating man who died.

text.p: Militant South Korean students on Friday admitted beating a suspected police spy who was found dead last month in the southwestern city of Kwangju.
A spokesman for the student council of Kwangju's Chunnam National University told reporters that council members had beaten Lee Jong-kwon, 25, during interrogation.
Police believe the beating was the cause of death.
"The police believe that Lee Jong-kwon was beaten to death by students who thought he was a police informant," a police officer said.
Police said they had detained two students and planned to arrest five others in connection with Lee's death.
If the police prove to be correct, Lee would be the second suspected police informer tortured to death by students within two weeks.
Last week the pro-Pyongyang Hanchongryon group took responsibility for the death of Lee Suk, a suspected police spy, who died as a direct result of beatings.
A hunger strike by 31 Hanchongryon students went into its second day on Friday at a Roman Catholic Church in central Seoul.
The students, who chained themselves to fence railings, are demanding an end to a government crackdown on the organisation.
